simple.meaning: שָׁאָה (shâʼâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to rush ; by implication, to desolate.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across 2 Kings, Isaiah, beginning at 2 Kings 19:25. Its contexts include mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁאָה (H7582).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

structuredEvidence.definition: to rush ; by implication, to desolate

firstOccurrence.englishText: Haven’t you heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.

timeline.evidenceText: Haven’t you heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it of ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.
Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.
“ ‘Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning them into ruinous heaps.

Niph`al Imperfect 3feminine singular שְׁמָמָה תִּשָּׁאֶה Isa 6:11 , usually, and the ground be ruined into a desolation, but ᵐ5 Lo Du Marti תִּשָּׁאֵר be left a desolation; 3 masculine plural יִשָּׁא֑וּן 17:12 they are in uproar (of nations, || יֶהֱמָיוּן ), 17:13 (but strike out as doublet Du Che Hpt Marti). H. in giving לְהַשְׁאוֺת as Qr, but see Baer Gi), to cause ... cities to crash into ruined heaps.
